questions.question: Write a brief description of First Come First Serve CPU Scheduling Algorithm.
questions.solution_html:
• Write a brief description of First Come First Serve (FCFS) CPU Scheduling Algorithm. FCFS is the simplest scheduling method where processes are executed in the order they arrive in the ready queue. It is non-preemptive and can lead to the “convoy effect.” Example: If processes arrive in order of burst time 10, 5, 2, the average waiting time can be high due to long jobs at the front. Definition

questions.question: Differentiate between programmed I/O, interrupt-driven I/O, and DMA, and evaluate which is most efficient in high-speed data transfer.
questions.solution_html: • Differentiate between Programmed I/O, Interrupt-driven I/O, and DMA, and evaluate which is most efficient in High-Speed Data Transfer. Programmed I/O: CPU actively waits for I/O completion. Interrupt-driven I/O: Device sends an interrupt when ready, freeing CPU time. DMA (Direct Memory Access): Data is transferred directly between memory and device without CPU involvement. Most efficient: DMA, especially for large data transfers. Definition of each I/O method- (3 marks) Comparative table or differences- (3 marks) Evaluation of efficiency with reason- (3 marks) Suitable application example- (1 mark) Total= (10 marks) END OF SCHEME
